PROCEDURE PERFORMED:
Ion robotic bronchoscopy
INDICATIONS:
1.9 cm right upper lobe apical indeterminate lung mass; underlying rheumatoid arthritis. Tissue diagnosis requested.
MEDICATIONS:
General anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway
IMAGING / CONFIRMATION:
DT; radial EBUS
TECHNICAL DIFFICULTY:
No
LIMITATIONS:
None
TOLERANCE:
Good after intervention
FINDINGS:
After informed consent and time-out, a therapeutic bronchoscope was introduced under general anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway. Airway inspection to the
first subsegmental level showed no obstructing endobronchial lesion. The Ion robotic platform was docked and a deliberate workflow with fluoroscopy, radial
EBUS, and cone-beam confirmation was performed. The target was a 1.9 cm lesion in the right upper lobe apical. Imaging confirmation used DT. Initial
fluoroscopy suggested near-target positioning. Radial probe EBUS demonstrated subtle concentric signal after catheter adjustment. A cone-beam or
tomographic spin was then obtained to assess tool-to-lesion relationship, after which the catheter was adjusted as needed and repeat fluoroscopy was
performed. Once tool-in-lesion or satisfactory tool-to-lesion relationship was confirmed, lesion sampling proceeded. Samples obtained included TBNA x5;
forceps biopsies x7; brushings x2; BAL x1; cryobiopsies x3. Technical difficulty: No. Limitation(s): None. Associated linear EBUS staging was then performed.
Surveyed stations included 11L (5.8 mm), 4L (6.4 mm), 7 (10.1 mm), 4R (7.2 mm). Sampled stations: 11L x4 (malignant cells on ROSE); 4L x3 (negative on
ROSE); 7 x4 (negative on ROSE). At the end of the case, the airway was reinspected, blood/secretions were suctioned, and there was no active bleeding.
ESTIMATED BLOOD LOSS:
<5 mL
COMPLICATIONS:
Brief bronchospasm treated with bronchodilator and deepening of anesthesia
IMPRESSION:
Successful ion robotic bronchoscopy targeting of the right upper lobe apical lesion. Associated EBUS staging was
performed. Minor immediate complication: brief bronchospasm treated with bronchodilator and deepening of
anesthesia.
RECOMMENDATIONS:
Recover in PACU; post-procedure chest radiograph per protocol; await final pathology; integrate EBUS staging into
treatment planning
CPT / ICD:
Synthetic only / synthetic only
Ion robotic bronchoscopy report

PROCEDURE: Ion robotic bronchoscopy
INDICATION: 3.3 cm right middle lobe PET-avid lesion; prior treated lung cancer. Tissue diagnosis requested.
ANESTHESIA: General anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway
After informed consent and time-out, a therapeutic bronchoscope was introduced under general anesthesia with laryngeal mask airway. Airway
inspection to the first subsegmental level showed no obstructing endobronchial lesion. The Ion robotic platform was docked and a deliberate workflow
with fluoroscopy, radial EBUS, and cone-beam confirmation was performed. The target was a 3.3 cm lesion in the right middle lobe. Imaging
confirmation used CBCT. Initial fluoroscopy suggested near-target positioning. Radial probe EBUS demonstrated no clear radial image but lesion
localization felt acceptable after fluoroscopic confirmation. A cone-beam or tomographic spin was then obtained to assess tool-to-lesion relationship,
after which the catheter was adjusted as needed and repeat fluoroscopy was performed. Once tool-in-lesion or satisfactory tool-to-lesion relationship
was confirmed, lesion sampling proceeded. Samples obtained included TBNA x4; forceps biopsies x9; brushings x2; BAL x1. Technical difficulty: No.
Limitation(s): None. Associated linear EBUS staging was then performed. Surveyed stations included 7 (10.1 mm), 4R (7.2 mm), 11R (8.9 mm), 10R (7.4
mm). Sampled stations: 7 x4 (no ROSE; cytology/cell block); 4R x3 (no ROSE; cytology/cell block); 11R x4 (no ROSE; cytology/cell block). At the end of
the case, the airway was reinspected, blood/secretions were suctioned, and there was no active bleeding.
EBL: <5 mL
COMPLICATIONS: Brief SVT during procedure, self-limited after anesthetic adjustment
IMPRESSION: Successful ion robotic bronchoscopy targeting of the right middle lobe lesion. Associated EBUS staging was performed. Minor immediate
complication: brief svt during procedure, self-limited after anesthetic adjustment.
PLAN: Recover in PACU; post-procedure chest radiograph per protocol; await final pathology; integrate EBUS staging into treatment planning

Right upper lobe adenocarcinoma.

PROCEDURES PERFORMED: Shape-sensing robotic bronchosocpy (Ion) w/ transbroncial bx and linear EBUS-TBNA. INDICATION: peripherl pulmonary opacity requiring tissue diagnosis before definitive therapy. TARGET: Preprocedure CT demonstrated a 33-mm ground-glass RML target associated with a positive bronchus sign and located about 18 mm from the pleural surface.
DETAILS: After informed consent and a procedural time-out, the patient was placed under general anesthesia via an 8.5-mm ETT. The tracheobronchial tree was inspected to the first subsegmental level. No endobroncial mass was identified. PEEP and tidal volume were optimized for peripheral navagation, and a breath hold was coordinated for 3D imaging; Navigation proceeded to the peripheral RB4 lateral airway. The catheter was locked after the system indicated proximity to the target. Intraprocedural CBCT was used for localization. Multiplanar reconstructions demonstrated the catheter adjacent to the target; after a 6 mm correction, needle position was confirmed within the lesion. rEBUS demonstrated an eccentric lesion pattern; the catheter was repositioned toward the maximal ultrasound signal before sampling. Tissue acquisition included 5 passes of transbronchial needle aspiration with a 21-gauge flexible needle, 2 1.1-mm transbronchial cryobiopsies, and bronchoalveolar lavage from the target segment (40 mL instilled, 20 mL returned). ROSE showed atypical epithelial cells; additional material was obtained for cell block and molecular testing.
STAGING: After peripheral sampling, linear EBUS was performed. Stations 11L, 7, 4R, 11R were identified and sampled with multiple needle passes where anatomically accessible. Nodal staging was completed in a systematic N3-to-N1 sequence relative to the target side.
COMPLICATIONS: No immediate procedural complication occurred. The patient was extubated in the procedure area and transferred to recovery in stable condition.
FINAL IMPRESSION: Successful Ion robotic-assisted bronchoscopy of a 33-mm ground-glass RML lesion with tissue acquisition.  Intraprocedural confirmation incorporated CBCT, with TIL confirmation documented. Systematic EBUS-TBNA staging was performed (11L, 7, 4R, 11R). No immediate complication.

PROCEDURES PERFORMED: Ion robotic navigational bronchoscopy and linear EBUS-TBNA.
INDICATION: persistent ground-glass lesion with interval enlargement.
TARGET: The target was a 25-mm ground-glass lesion in the Lingula (LB4 superior lingular); bronchus sign was positive, and the closest pleural distance on the planning CT was approximately 13 mm.

DETAILS: A time-out was completed and general anesth with neuromuscular blockade and endotracheal intubation was established. Conventional bronchoscopy was performed first for airway inspection. The robotic catheter was subsequently introduced and registration to the CT-derived pathway was satisfactory. Ventilation was kept stable during navigation; no special recruitment maneuver was required. Navigation proceeded to the peripherl LB4 superior lingular airway. The catheter was locked after the system indicated proximity to the target. Ion-integrated tomosythesis was used for intraprocedural target update and tool-in-lesion confirmation. The final trajectory was satisfactory on orthogonal fluoroscopic views. rEBUS demonstrated a concentric view corresponding to the target. Tissue acquisition included 7 passes of transbronchil needle aspiration with a 21-gauge flexible needle, 6 transbronchial forceps bx, bronchial brushing for cytlogy, and bronchoalveolar lavage from the target segment (60 mL instilled, 26 mL returned). ROSE was not available.

STAGING: After peripheral sampling, linear EBUS was performed. Stations 4R, 7, 4L, 10L were identified and sampled with multiple needle passes where anatomically accessible. Specimens were sent separately for cytology/cell block.

COMPLICATIONS: Hemostasis was excellent. The patient tolerated the procedure without immediate complication.

FINAL IMPRESSION: Successful Ion robotic-assisted bronchoscopy of a 25-mm ground-glass Lingula lesion with tissue acquisition. Intraprocedural confirmation incorporated DT, with tool-in-lesion confirmation documented. Systematic EBUS-TBNA staging was performed (4R, 7, 4L, 10L). No immediate complication.

[BRONCH NOTE] Robotic-assisted bronchscopy using the Ion Endoluminal System and linear EBUS-TBNA
[PRE/POST DX] new perihperal pulmonary lesion in a patient with prior malignacy. The target was a 10-mm ground-glass lesion in the RUL (RB1 apical); bronchus sign was negative, and the closest pleural distance on the planning CT was approximately 27 mm.

Initial flexible bronchoscopy demonstrated normal major airways aside from scant secretions, which were therapeutically aspirated. The Ion platform was registered and the planned pathway was reviewed. PEEP and tidal volume were optimized for peripheral navigation, and a breath hold was coordinated for 3D imaging. Ion-integrated tomosynthesis was used for intraprocedural target update and tool in lesion confirmation. Intraprocedural confirmation incorporated DT, with tool in lesion confirmation documented. Systematic EBUS-TBNA staging was performed (4L, 7, 4R, 11R). Immediate adverse event: pneumothorax pigtail.

text:
Procedure
Robotic-assisted bronchoscopy using the Ion Endoluminal System and linear EBUS-TBNA

Indication
spiculated pulmonary nodule with interval growth. Target characteristics: RLL RB10 posterior basal, 15 mm, solid; bronchus sign negative; pleural distance approximately 6 mm.

Narrative
Following induction of general anesthesia with a cuffed endotracheal tube, a standard airway survey showed patent central airways without an obstructing endobronchial lesion. The Ion robotic bronchoscopy system was then docked and registered to the preprocedure CT plan. A recruitment maneuver was performed after intubation and again before lesion confirmation imaging. Using shape-sensing navigation, the catheter was advanced through RB10 posterior basal to within approximately 10 mm of the planned lesion center. DT identified approximately 12 mm of CT-to-body divergence. After the Ion target was updated, a mobile 3D spin confirmed the forceps and needle trajectory through the target. Radial EBUS did not produce a definitive lesional view despite two airway positions; sampling proceeded based on updated 3D/fluoroscopic localization. Tissue acquisition included 6 passes of transbronchial needle aspiration with a 21-gauge flexible needle, and 9 transbronchial forceps biopsies. ROSE showed lesional cells suspicious for malignancy.

Nodal Evaluation
After peripheral sampling, linear EBUS was performed. Stations 4L, 7, 4R, 11R were identified and sampled with multiple needle passes where anatomically accessible. Nodal staging was completed in a systematic N3-to-N1 sequence relative to the target side.

Complication
Estimated blood loss was minimal. No pneumothorax was seen on final imaging.

Impression
Successful Ion robotic-assisted bronchoscopy of a 15-mm solid RLL lesion with tissue acquisition. Intraprocedural confirmation incorporated mCBCT+DT, with tool-in-lesion confirmation documented. Systematic EBUS-TBNA staging was performed (4L, 7, 4R, 11R). No immediate complication.

text:
PROCEDURE
Robotic-assisted bronchoscopy using the Ion Endoluminal System

INDICATION
new peripheral pulmonary lesion in a patient with prior malignancy. The target was a 29-mm solid lesion in the RLL (RB7 medial basal); bronchus sign was positive, and the closest pleural distance on the planning CT was approximately 20 mm.

FINDINGS AND TECHNIQUE
After informed consent and a procedural time-out, the patient was placed under general anesthesia with neuromuscular blockade and endotracheal intubation. The tracheobronchial tree was inspected to the first subsegmental level. No endobronchial mass was identified. Ventilation was adjusted to limit atelectasis during navigation, with recruitment performed before advanced imaging. The Ion catheter was advanced along the preplanned airway route to the RB7 medial basal lesion. Catheter articulation remained stable during tool exchanges. DT identified approximately 13 mm of CT-to-body divergence. After the Ion target was updated, a mobile 3D spin confirmed the forceps and needle trajectory through the target. Radial EBUS did not produce a definitive lesional view despite two airway positions; sampling proceeded based on updated 3D/fluoroscopic localization. Tissue acquisition included 6 passes of transbronchial needle aspiration with a 21-gauge flexible needle, 3 1.1-mm transbronchial cryobiopsies, and bronchoalveolar lavage from the target segment (60 mL instilled, 27 mL returned). ROSE demonstrated predominantly macrophages and bronchial cells without definite malignancy.

EBUS STAGING
No mediastinal or hilar EBUS-TBNA was performed.

COMPLICATIONS
Transient hypotension occurred during prolonged image acquisition and responded to anesthetic adjustment and a brief vasopressor bolus. There was no associated bleeding or arrhythmia.

IMPRESSION
Successful Ion robotic-assisted bronchoscopy of a 29-mm solid RLL lesion with tissue acquisition. Intraprocedural confirmation incorporated mCBCT+DT, with tool-in-lesion confirmation documented. No linear EBUS staging was performed. Immediate adverse event: transient hypotension.

PROCEDURE
Ion robotic navigational bronchoscopy

INDICATION
enlarging pulmonary nodule concerning for primary lung malignancy. The target was a 33-mm solid lesion in the RLL (RB7 medial basal); bronchus sign was positive, and the closest pleural distance on the planning CT was approximately 13 mm.

indeterminate pulmonary nodule with elevated clinical probability of malignancy. Target characteristics: RLL RB9 lateral basal, 11 mm, ground-glass; bronchus sign positive; pleural distance approximately 19 mm.

Radial EBUS demonstrated an eccentric lesion pattern; the catheter was repositioned toward the maximal ultrasound signal before sampling. After peripheral sampling, linear EBUS was performed. Stations 11L, 4L, 7, 4R, 11R were identified and sampled with multiple needle passes where anatomically accessible. Specimens were sent separately for cytology/cell block.

Complication
Hemostasis was excellent. The patient tolerated the procedure without immediate complication.

Impression
Successful Ion robotic-assisted bronchoscopy of a 11-mm ground-glass RLL lesion with tissue acquisition. Intraprocedural confirmation incorporated CBCT, with tool-in-lesion confirmation documented. Systematic EBUS-TBNA staging was performed (11L, 4L, 7, 4R, 11R). No immediate complication.

Linear endobronchial ultrasound bronchoscopy with EBUS-TBNA

Clinical Indication
necrotic subcarinal adenopathy with concern for infection or malignancy

Sedation and Airway
General anesthesia was maintained using a size 5 supraglottic airway.

The tracheobronchial tree was inspected to the first subsegmental level; only scant clear secretions were present. A linear EBUS bronchoscope was then introduced. Sampling was intentionally limited to the radiographically or clinically abnormal target stations rather than a complete lung-cancer staging examination. Station 7 (25 mm, round, heterogeneous, with a focal coagulation necrosis sign) was sampled with 3 passes. Additional stations visualized but not sampled included 12L (15 mm) because of small size/benign morphology or low incremental yield. EBUS-TBNA was performed with a 22G needle. ROSE demonstrated necrotic material with inflammatory cells; additional specimens were sent for microbiology and cell block. Additional material was submitted for AFB and fungal studies.

Sampling
Samples from each station were labeled separately. Primary specimen handling included cytology smears, cell block, AFB culture, fungal culture.

Immediate Complications
The LMA shifted during scope manipulation, producing a brief desaturation. The supraglottic airway was repositioned with immediate improvement in ventilation and oxygenation; the remainder of the procedure was uncomplicated.

Assessment
Adequate targeted nodal tissue was obtained for cytology and ancillary testing where indicated.
